hero.headline: Trump warns Iran will pay the price as negotiations stall
hero.teaser: President Trump threatened consequences for Iran following attacks on U.S. allies Kuwait and Bahrain as nuclear negotiations drag on.
hero.body:
President Trump warned Iran on Wednesday morning that it will not get away with attacks on U.S. allies Kuwait and Bahrain. He posted on Truth Social that Iran has taken too long to negotiate a deal that would have been great for them, and now they will have to pay the price.

The warning comes as gas prices remain stuck above $4 per gallon. The stalled negotiations and regional tensions have contributed to sustained pressure on energy markets, affecting American consumers at the pump.

cards.headline: Inflation rises above 4% for first time in three years as gasoline prices surge
cards.body:
Consumer inflation has climbed to its highest level in more than three years, topping 4% as gasoline prices spiked following military actions in the Middle East. The increase marks a significant reversal in the downward trajectory of price growth that had characterized recent years.

Before the conflict began, inflation was at 2.4% in February. Prices have increased sharply over the past several months, rising to 3.3% in March before moving up to 3.8% in April and reaching 4.2% in May. The surge in fuel costs has been driven by disruptions in global energy markets after the United States and Israel launched military operations against Iran. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has affected energy prices significantly. Gasoline prices have risen sharply in response to concerns about oil supply stability in the region, directly pushing up the overall inflation rate.

The national average gas price stands at about $4.16 per gallon, approximately $1 more expensive than the same time last year, though down $0.37 from a month earlier.

The 4% threshold represents a meaningful milestone for American consumers and policymakers. Inflation had been gradually declining over the past three years, and the sudden reversal puts renewed pressure on household budgets. Higher prices at the pump affect not only transportation costs but also the price of goods that depend on shipping and delivery.

The Federal Reserve and economic policymakers now face fresh challenges in managing price stability. The central bank has spent years working to bring inflation down from its peak, and this new spike complicates those efforts. The extent to which the increase reflects temporary supply disruptions versus more persistent inflationary pressures remains to be seen.

This represents the third consecutive monthly increase since the start of the Iran war, indicating a troubling trend rather than a one-time spike. The trajectory suggests that ongoing tensions in the Middle East continue to have substantial economic consequences for American households.

Consumers across the country are likely to feel the effects in their daily spending, particularly those who drive regularly for work or family obligations. The broader economic implications will depend on how long gasoline prices remain elevated and whether the inflationary pressure spreads to other sectors of the economy beyond energy costs.

The situation presents a complex challenge for policymakers who must balance the need to control inflation while accounting for external geopolitical factors that are driving current price increases. Officials will be monitoring whether the price surge represents a temporary disruption tied to Middle Eastern developments or signals a more fundamental shift in inflation dynamics.

cards.headline: Trump signs immigration enforcement bill into law
cards.teaser: President Trump signed the Secure America Act into law Wednesday morning, finalizing a GOP-led reconciliation package that funds U.S.
cards.body:
President Trump signed the Secure America Act into law Wednesday morning, a GOP-led reconciliation package that funds U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Border Patrol through 2029. The nearly $70 billion bill passed the House on Tuesday and advanced in the Senate on Friday after weeks of negotiations among Republican leadership and party members.

The legislation allocates resources for personnel, detention facilities, and operational costs for both ICE and Border Patrol over the four-year period. Republicans argued the multi-year funding structure provides enforcement agencies with stable resources to conduct border security operations without relying on annual appropriations battles. Democrats opposed the package, citing concerns that the reconciliation process bypassed normal committee review and debate procedures.

cards.headline: Federal Reserve Faces Pressure on Interest Rates as Inflation Data Arrives
cards.teaser: New economic figures are putting investors on edge over the prospect of rate increases to counter rising prices.
cards.body:
Investors are bracing for potential Federal Reserve action following the release of inflation data that showed consumer prices climbing to levels not seen in three years. The figures have raised expectations that the central bank may need to raise interest rates to prevent further price acceleration.

Markets have shown increased volatility as traders position for possible policy changes. Higher interest rates would make borrowing more expensive for consumers and businesses, potentially slowing economic growth but helping to control inflation that has been driven partly by energy cost increases.

cards.headline: Ukraine Strikes Russian Military Plant and Oil Facilities
cards.teaser: Ukrainian forces hit a military manufacturing facility deep inside Russia, along with an oil refinery and a tanker in the Black Sea.
cards.body:
Ukraine's military reported striking a Russian military plant that produces drone components deep inside Russia, along with attacks on oil infrastructure. The strikes targeted an oil refinery and a "shadow fleet" oil tanker in the Black Sea. Ukraine stated that its missiles successfully hit the military manufacturing facility, which supplies key components for Russian drones used in the conflict.

The attacks caused fires at multiple oil facilities in Russia and Crimea. Russia characterized the strike on St. Petersburg as unprecedented in scale.

cards.headline: Iran Vows Retaliation After US Strikes
cards.teaser: Tehran said it would respond to any attacks following an exchange of strikes with the United States.
cards.body:
Iran vowed retaliation after the United States launched strikes, escalating tensions between the two countries. President Trump warned that Iran would "pay the price" for taking too long to negotiate an agreement to end the conflict.

The exchange of strikes followed the downing of a helicopter near the Strait of Hormuz. The Iranian government said it would respond to any attacks on its territory or interests, raising concerns about further escalation in a conflict involving American allies across the region.

cards.headline: SpaceX Prepares for Stock Market Debut as Demand Builds
cards.teaser: The space exploration company is moving forward with its initial public offering as investors position for the debut.
cards.body:
SpaceX is preparing for its stock market debut, with demand for shares in the initial public offering reportedly approaching four times oversubscription. The offering represents one of the largest technology IPOs in recent years and has generated significant interest from both institutional and individual investors.

The company's president, Gwynne Shotwell, has been instrumental in executing the business strategy that transformed SpaceX into a $1.75 trillion enterprise. Some investors are adjusting their portfolios ahead of the offering, anticipating potential market volatility when trading begins.

hero.headline: Ukraine Strikes Russian Military Plant and Oil Facilities
hero.teaser: Ukrainian forces hit a military manufacturing facility deep inside Russia, along with an oil refinery and a tanker in the Black Sea.
hero.body:
Ukraine's military reported striking a Russian military plant that produces drone components deep inside Russia, along with attacks on oil infrastructure. The strikes targeted an oil refinery and a "shadow fleet" oil tanker in the Black Sea. The attacks caused fires at multiple oil facilities in Russia and Crimea. Russia characterized the strike on St. Petersburg as unprecedented in scale.

cards.headline: Hong Kong Files Charges Over Apartment Fire That Killed 168
cards.teaser: Authorities charged seven people and two companies over a blaze at Wang Fuk Court, the deadliest fire in Hong Kong in 70 years.
cards.body:
Hong Kong prosecutors have filed 25 charges including manslaughter and conspiracy against seven individuals and two companies following an apartment fire at Wang Fuk Court that killed 168 people. The charges mark the first to emerge from an investigation into the blaze, which was the deadliest fire Hong Kong has experienced in 70 years.

The monthslong investigation examined the causes of the fire and identified those responsible for the conditions that resulted in the significant loss of life.

cards.headline: At Least 12 Killed in Johannesburg Shooting
cards.teaser: Multiple attackers stormed a community of tin shacks in Johannesburg, killing at least 12 people in a mass shooting.
cards.body:
Police in Johannesburg said they were searching for more than 10 attackers who carried out a shooting that left at least 12 people dead. The attackers stormed a community of tin shacks, opening fire on residents.

Investigators were still working to determine the motive behind the attack. The police launched a manhunt for the suspects, who fled the scene after the shooting. The incident represents one of the deadliest mass shootings in recent South African history.

cards.headline: Violence Erupts in Belfast After Stabbing Attack
cards.teaser: Cars and a bus were set on fire and families were driven from their homes after video of a stabbing circulated online.
cards.body:
Belfast and other UK cities experienced violence following a street stabbing. A Sudanese man was arrested in connection with a stabbing attack on a Belfast street. Video of the incident circulated widely on social media and was amplified by far-right activists, triggering protests.

The unrest spread beyond Belfast. In Glasgow, police arrested three people over violence and racist assaults that occurred after the video spread. Members of the public were attacked because of their skin color. UK leaders called for calm as the disturbances continued across multiple locations.

cards.headline: Senior Russian Military Officer Killed
cards.teaser: The death of a high-ranking Russian officer appeared to be the latest in a series of targeted assassinations inside Russia.
cards.body:
A senior Russian military officer died in what appeared to be a targeted killing. The death added to a string of assassinations of high-profile opponents of Ukraine operating inside Russian territory.

The pattern of killings has targeted individuals involved in military operations or propaganda efforts.

cards.headline: Japan Objects to Trump's Use of Anime Characters
cards.teaser: The president angered some fans by using images of characters like Pikachu and Naruto without authorization.
cards.body:
President Trump has used images of popular anime characters including Pikachu and Naruto, sparking backlash in Japan. The characters appear in what seem to be political or promotional materials.

Japanese fans have criticized the use on social media, raising concerns about intellectual property rights and cultural respect. The incident has prompted debate about whether the characters were used with proper authorization from their creators.

cards.headline: Iran Vows Retaliation After US Strikes
cards.teaser: Tehran said it would respond to any attacks following an exchange of strikes with the United States.
cards.body:
Iran vowed retaliation after the United States launched strikes, escalating tensions between the two countries. President Trump warned that Iran would "pay the price" for taking too long to negotiate an agreement to end the conflict.

The exchange of strikes followed the downing of a helicopter near the Strait of Hormuz. The Iranian government said it would respond to any attacks on its territory or interests, raising concerns about further escalation in a conflict involving American allies across the region.

cards.headline: Federal judge disqualifies lawyers on both sides of case for AI-generated fake citations
cards.teaser: A federal judge removed all attorneys from a lawsuit after discovering both sides submitted legal briefs citing nonexistent cases created by artificial intelligence.
cards.body:
A federal judge took the rare step of disqualifying lawyers representing both parties in a lawsuit after learning they had used artificial intelligence tools that generated citations to fake cases in their legal filings. The judge canceled the scheduled trial and kicked all involved attorneys off the case.

The decision highlights growing concerns about the misuse of AI in legal practice. Lawyers on both sides failed to catch that their briefs referenced fabricated case law, demonstrating a breakdown in professional responsibility. The sanctions represent a significant consequence for attorneys who rely on AI-generated content without proper verification.

cards.headline: Nancy Mace loses South Carolina Republican primary for governor
cards.teaser: Republican Representative Nancy Mace suffered a decisive defeat in the South Carolina gubernatorial primary, with Evette and Wilson advancing to a runoff.
cards.body:
Nancy Mace, once considered a rising political figure, lost the Republican primary election for South Carolina governor. Pamela Evette and Wilson will advance to a runoff after neither secured a majority in the primary contest.

The loss marks a significant setback for Mace, who had been viewed as an ascending voice within the Republican Party. Senator Lindsey Graham secured his party's nomination in a separate race during the same primary election night.

cards.headline: Severe storms knock out power to thousands across Minnesota
cards.teaser: Strong winds and thunderstorms downed trees and left up to 50,000 customers without electricity in the Twin Cities metro area and across Minnesota.
cards.body:
Severe weather moved through Minnesota early in the morning, bringing strong winds that toppled trees and damaged power infrastructure. As many as 50,000 customers in the Twin Cities area lost electricity, with thousands more affected statewide.

The storms caused widespread damage across the region. A train derailment occurred near Hoffman, though the connection to storm conditions has not been specified. Utility crews worked to restore power throughout the affected areas as residents dealt with blocked roads and property damage from fallen trees.

cards.headline: Trump and Iran exchange threats after military strikes
cards.teaser: President Trump warned Iran would face consequences for delays in reaching a deal, while Tehran vowed retaliation following recent attacks.
cards.body:
President Trump warned Iran it "will have to pay the price" for delaying a deal, following U.S. strikes against Iranian targets. The warning came after a helicopter was downed Monday near the Strait of Hormuz, prompting the military exchange between the two countries.

Iran responded by vowing retaliation for any attacks on its territory. The escalating threats between Washington and Tehran underscore rising tensions and complicate prospects for diplomatic negotiations between the nations.

cards.headline: Ukraine strikes military plant deep inside Russia with missiles
cards.teaser: Ukrainian forces hit a military manufacturing facility far from the border, along with an oil refinery and tanker in the Black Sea.
cards.body:
Ukraine's military says it struck a military plant deep inside Russian territory, along with a Russian oil refinery and a "shadow fleet" oil tanker in the Black Sea. The coordinated attacks targeted Russian energy and military infrastructure.

These strikes are part of Ukraine's broader campaign to disrupt Russia's supply chains. By targeting fuel production and transport, Kyiv has made it increasingly difficult for Moscow to deliver military and civilian supplies to occupied territories.

cards.headline: Three arrested in Glasgow for racist assaults following Belfast knife attack
cards.teaser: Police Scotland arrested three people after members of the public were attacked based on the color of their skin during unrest tied to a Belfast incident.
cards.body:
Police Scotland arrested three people following unrest in Glasgow on Tuesday evening. Members of the public were attacked because of their skin color during the disorder.

The incidents occurred in the aftermath of a knife attack in Belfast, which prompted protests and disturbances across multiple cities.

hero.headline: US Inflation Climbs to 4.2%, Highest Rate in Three Years
hero.body:
Consumer prices rose 4.2 percent in May compared to a year earlier, marking the highest annual inflation rate in three years, according to recent data releases. The increase represents the third consecutive monthly rise since the start of the conflict between the US and Israel with Iran.

The acceleration in price growth has been driven largely by energy costs. Before the conflict began in February, inflation was running at 2.4 percent. Since then, prices have jumped sharply, rising to 3.3 percent in March and 3.8 percent in April before reaching 4.2 percent in May. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz and military tensions have disrupted oil markets and pushed fuel prices higher, affecting consumers across multiple spending categories from gasoline to transportation costs.

The latest data comes from the personal consumption expenditures price index, a key measure of inflation watched closely by the Federal Reserve. According to Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union, Americans are facing mounting financial pressure. "Inflation is at a three-year high and personal savings has cratered to one of the lowest levels in the past 20 years," Long said. "Many Americans are spending more than the income they have coming in. This is not sustainable, especially for lower-income and middle-class households."

The inflation report puts the Federal Reserve in a challenging position as policymakers consider whether to raise interest rates to combat rising prices. However, there are signs that oil prices may moderate. According to reports, the United States and Iran have reached an outline agreement to extend their ceasefire for 60 days and launch negotiations on Iran's nuclear program, though President Trump has yet to give final approval. Oil prices dropped back from earlier highs following these reports.

The jump in inflation contrasts with economic growth data, which showed the US economy expanded more slowly than initially thought at the start of the year. GDP grew at an annual rate of 1.6 percent, down from the 2 percent previously estimated.

The current surge in inflation represents a reversal of recent progress in bringing price increases under control. Economists are watching closely to see whether price increases spread beyond energy into other sectors of the economy, which would signal broader inflationary pressure. The Federal Reserve has previously indicated it would respond to sustained inflation with tighter monetary policy, though officials have not yet commented on the latest data.

Investors had shown volatility ahead of the inflation report release, with market movements reflecting uncertainty about how policymakers will respond to the elevated inflation readings.

cards.headline: Stocks Fall and Oil Prices Jump Following Middle East Strikes
cards.teaser: Markets reacted sharply to renewed military action that threatened a recent cease-fire between the United States and Iran.
cards.body:
Stock markets across Asia fell as a tech sell-off coincided with renewed military exchanges between Iran and Israel. Oil prices became volatile in response to the escalating tensions, with energy traders sensitive to any developments in the conflict.

The attacks disrupted a two-month cease-fire involving Iran and the United States. President Trump warned Iran would "have to pay the price" for delaying deal negotiations, while Tehran vowed to retaliate against any further strikes. The cycle of threats and counterattacks has left markets uncertain about regional stability and global energy supplies.

cards.headline: Cybersecurity Startup Cyera Raises $600 Million, Valued at $12 Billion
cards.teaser: The five-year-old company focuses on data security for artificial intelligence applications.
cards.body:
Cyera, a cybersecurity firm specializing in protection for the artificial intelligence era, has raised $600 million in new funding. The investment round values the company at $12 billion, reflecting strong investor interest in security solutions tailored to AI systems.

The five-year-old startup has positioned itself at the intersection of two major technology trends: the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence and growing concerns about data protection. The funding will support the company's continued development of security tools designed specifically for organizations deploying AI technologies.

cards.headline: SpaceX Prepares for Stock Market Debut as Demand Builds
cards.teaser: The space exploration company is moving forward with its initial public offering as investors position for the debut.
cards.body:
SpaceX is preparing for its stock market debut, with demand for shares in the initial public offering reportedly approaching four times oversubscription. The offering represents one of the largest technology IPOs in recent years and has generated significant interest from both institutional and individual investors.

The company's president, Gwynne Shotwell, has been instrumental in executing the business strategy that transformed SpaceX into a $1.75 trillion enterprise. Some investors are adjusting their portfolios ahead of the offering, anticipating potential market volatility when trading begins.

cards.headline: Stock Markets Open Lower on Technology Weakness and Geopolitical Tension
cards.teaser: Major indexes declined at the opening bell as investors weighed multiple economic and political factors.
cards.body:
US stock markets opened lower, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average falling 500 points as investors reacted to developments in the Middle East and awaited inflation data. Technology stocks showed particular weakness, contributing to the broader market decline.

The combination of renewed military strikes between the United States and Iran, along with anticipation of consumer price figures, created uncertainty for traders. Futures markets had signaled the downturn before regular trading began, reflecting concerns about both geopolitical stability and domestic economic policy.

cards.headline: Technology Companies Shift AI Pricing Strategies as Costs Mount
cards.teaser: Major tech firms are moving away from unlimited AI usage models as expenses prove higher than anticipated.
cards.body:
Large technology companies are quietly revising their artificial intelligence pricing strategies, moving away from all-you-can-eat models toward usage-based billing as the costs of running AI systems exceed initial projections. The shift represents a significant change in how the industry packages and sells AI services to customers.

Several reports indicate that AI operations are proving more expensive than the human labor they were designed to replace, at least in the near term. Companies that initially offered unlimited AI access are now implementing metered pricing to better align revenue with the actual computational costs of providing the services.

hero.headline: Fusion startup Avalanche Energy heats plasma past 10 million degrees in desktop reactor
hero.body:
Avalanche Energy announced that its fusion reactor prototype heated plasma to temperatures exceeding 10 million degrees Celsius, a significant achievement for the startup developing compact fusion technology. The milestone was reached using a desktop-sized reactor, demonstrating progress in the company's effort to create smaller and more accessible fusion power systems.

This temperature achievement matters because fusion reactions require extremely high heat to force atomic nuclei to overcome their natural repulsion and merge together. Most large experimental fusion reactors need temperatures exceeding 100 million degrees Celsius to sustain fusion reactions that produce net energy output. By comparison, the sun's core, where fusion naturally occurs, reaches approximately 15 million degrees Celsius.

Avalanche Energy is one of several private fusion startups pursuing alternatives to massive government-funded projects like ITER in France. The company's strategy centers on building smaller, potentially more practical fusion devices that could be manufactured and deployed faster than traditional large-scale reactors. If successful, desktop or room-sized fusion reactors could enable distributed power generation across multiple locations.

The fusion energy sector has drawn substantial investment as companies compete to demonstrate commercially viable fusion power. Various startups and research institutions have announced progress in recent years, though no fusion reactor has yet consistently produced more energy than it consumes on a commercial basis. Conventional fusion approaches such as tokamaks and stellarators require enormous facilities and powerful magnetic fields to contain the superheated plasma needed for reactions.

The fusion energy space has also attracted attention from major technology and business figures. Google's parent company Alphabet, OpenAI's Sam Altman, and other prominent investors have backed fusion companies as artificial intelligence and data centers create growing demand for clean energy sources. This investment wave reflects broader recognition that new energy solutions are becoming critical infrastructure.

Avalanche Energy has not publicly disclosed whether the plasma remained at these extreme temperatures or for how long the reaction was sustained. The company has also not released information about the energy balance of the reactor or its timeline for achieving commercial viability. These details would be crucial for assessing whether the technology can eventually generate more power than it consumes.

The startup joins numerous other fusion companies working on different reactor designs, each attempting to solve the engineering and physics challenges that have made fusion power commercially viable. The technology remains in early stages despite decades of research, and scientists remain divided on whether fusion can be produced economically at scale.

Avalanche Energy's announcement represents another data point in the ongoing race to commercialize fusion energy, though significant technical hurdles remain before any company demonstrates a practical, profit-generating fusion power plant.

cards.headline: Former SpaceX employees launch Ambrosia Energy to power AI data centers with solar and batteries
cards.teaser: Two SpaceX alumni founded an energy company aiming to build power plants faster and cheaper than natural gas facilities.
cards.body:
Ambrosia Energy, founded by two former SpaceX employees, is building solar and battery power plants designed to be constructed in under 12 months while offering costs competitive with natural gas generation. The startup is targeting the surging electricity demand from AI data centers.

The company plans to expand its generation capacity to gigawatts by 2030, entering a market where AI computing facilities are driving unprecedented demand for reliable power infrastructure.

cards.headline: Automakers enter energy storage business as AI drives electricity demand
cards.teaser: Companies including GM and Ford are moving into the energy storage sector as data centers strain power grids.
cards.body:
Electricity demand from AI data centers is pushing automakers like General Motors and Ford into the energy storage business. The shift reflects how AI computing infrastructure is creating new business opportunities beyond traditional industry boundaries.

The move by automotive manufacturers into energy storage comes as data centers supporting AI workloads require massive amounts of reliable power. Companies across sectors are responding to grid constraints and the need for distributed energy resources to meet rising electricity consumption.

cards.headline: Decart launches real-time world model for autonomous vehicle testing
cards.teaser: The company released Oasis 3, which generates photorealistic driving environments for testing self-driving systems.
cards.body:
Decart has launched Oasis 3, a real-time world model that generates photorealistic driving environments for autonomous vehicle testing. The tool is now available through an API for developers to build applications on.

The system allows autonomous vehicle developers to test their systems in varied driving scenarios through simulation, potentially accelerating development cycles and reducing costs compared to physical testing deployments.

cards.headline: Waymo develops new benchmark for comparing robotaxi safety to human drivers
cards.teaser: The autonomous vehicle company created a computer model to analyze human behavior in crash scenarios.
cards.body:
Waymo has created a new computer model designed to better understand how humans behave in crash scenarios that its robotaxis encounter on the road. This benchmark aims to provide more accurate comparisons between autonomous vehicle safety and human driver performance.

The model addresses a fundamental challenge in autonomous vehicle development: establishing whether self-driving systems are genuinely safer than human drivers. By using simulation to predict human responses in real-world driving situations, Waymo has developed a standardized method for evaluating and comparing safety performance.

cards.headline: Jedify raises $24 million to provide business context for AI agents
cards.teaser: The funding round was led by Norwest with participation from multiple venture firms and Snowflake Ventures.
cards.body:
Jedify secured $24 million in a funding round led by Norwest, with participation from S Capital VC, Cerca Partners, and Oceans Ventures. Snowflake Ventures joined as a strategic investor.

The company helps businesses equip AI agents with contextual information about their operations. This enables AI systems to access internal knowledge and processes needed for tasks like customer service and data analysis.

cards.headline: Snapchat restricts Spotlight sharing for users under 16 to friends only
cards.teaser: The social media platform is creating a separate profile system for younger users to limit content visibility.
cards.body:
Snapchat has implemented a new profile system for users under 16, restricting how they share content on the platform. These younger users can now only share Stories and Spotlight posts with friends they follow back, preventing their content from reaching the broader Snapchat community.

The change specifically targets Spotlight, Snapchat's short-form video feature. By limiting visibility to mutual connections only, the platform is narrowing the distribution of content created by underage users.

hero.headline: Staal scores on stomach to even Stanley Cup Final
hero.body:
Jordan Staal scored while stretched out on his stomach to lift the Carolina Hurricanes to a 5-3 victory over the Vegas Golden Knights, tying the Stanley Cup Final at two games apiece. Staal netted his second goal of the game on the decisive play that put the Hurricanes ahead for good.

The Hurricanes bounced back after falling behind in the series to even the championship matchup. The win keeps Carolina's Stanley Cup hopes alive as the series shifts back to Vegas for Game 5. Staal's performance anchored the Hurricanes' offensive effort in the critical win.

The Stanley Cup Final now stands deadlocked with three games remaining in the best-of-seven series. Both teams have won their home games thus far, setting up a pivotal stretch as the series continues. The Golden Knights will look to regain momentum when they host the next game.

Staal's unusual goal came at a crucial moment for the Hurricanes, who needed a win to avoid falling into a 3-1 series deficit. The center's two-goal performance highlighted Carolina's resilience in a must-win situation. The Hurricanes' victory keeps the championship within reach as they pursue their second Stanley Cup title in franchise history.

The series continues with Game 5 in Vegas as both teams battle for hockey's ultimate prize. With the Final now tied, neither team holds an advantage heading into the final stretch of the championship series.

cards.headline: Montgomery homers in 10th inning of major league debut
cards.teaser: Braden Montgomery hit a two-run homer in extra innings during his first major league game to rally the White Sox past the Braves.
cards.body:
Braden Montgomery delivered an unforgettable start to his major league career, hitting a two-run homer in the 10th inning to lift the Chicago White Sox past the Atlanta Braves 6-5. The walk-off blast capped a rousing debut for the rookie.

Montgomery's dramatic home run proved to be the difference in the extra-innings contest, giving the White Sox the comeback victory in his first game in the majors.

cards.headline: Chisholm homers to silence Cleveland crowd, lift Yankees
cards.teaser: Jazz Chisholm answered chants from the Cleveland crowd with an eighth-inning home run that gave the Yankees a victory over the Guardians.
cards.body:
Jazz Chisholm responded to chants of 'overrated' at Cleveland's ballpark by hitting an eighth-inning home run to give the New York Yankees a 3-2 win over the Guardians. The homer silenced the hostile crowd and provided the winning margin for the Yankees.

Chisholm's clutch hit came after Cleveland fans had been taunting him throughout the game. The Yankees outfielder delivered when it mattered most, sending his team to victory on the road.

cards.headline: USWNT edges Brazil as hosts finish with nine players
cards.teaser: The United States women's national team secured a 1-0 win over Brazil in a physical match that saw the hosts receive eight red cards.
cards.body:
Sophia Wilson's own goal in the second half secured a 1-0 victory for the United States over Brazil in Fortaleza. The match descended into chaos, with Brazil receiving eight red cards total and finishing with nine players on the field.

The disciplinary issues extended beyond the players. Brazil's head coach Arthur Elias and three staff members were sent off toward the end of the second half. After the final whistle, riot police surrounded match officials on the pitch as further confrontations erupted. U.S. manager Emma Hayes called it "an experience I will never forget."

cards.headline: Wembanyama avoids flagrant foul for shove on Brunson
cards.teaser: Victor Wembanyama will not receive a flagrant foul for his shove to the upper body of Jalen Brunson during a playoff game.
cards.body:
San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama will not face a flagrant foul for shoving New York Knicks guard Jalen Brunson during Game 3. The NBA reviewed the play and determined it did not warrant the flagrant classification.

The ruling means Wembanyama escapes additional penalties beyond the common foul called in the game, allowing him to remain available for the remainder of the playoff series.

cards.headline: Big 12 athletic directors challenge Sorsby eligibility ruling
cards.teaser: Athletic directors from Big 12 schools united to express opposition to a ruling that would allow Texas Tech quarterback Brendan Sorsby to play next season.
cards.body:
Big 12 athletic directors participated in a spirited call Tuesday with commissioner Brett Yormark to express their unified opposition to Texas Tech quarterback Brendan Sorsby's eligibility for next season. The ADs made clear their collective stance on the matter.

Despite the conference's pushback, Sorsby appears set to play for the Red Raiders, positioning Texas Tech as a top contender in the Big 12.

cards.headline: Pochettino says U.S. can win World Cup without top-ranked players
cards.teaser: United States men's national team coach Mauricio Pochettino believes his team can win the World Cup despite lacking players ranked in the top 100.
cards.body:
Mauricio Pochettino believes the United States men's national team can capture the World Cup championship despite having no players ranked in the top 100. The coach is emphasizing team strategy and cohesion over individual star talent as the Americans pursue their first World Cup title.

The U.S. will host the 2026 World Cup, and Pochettino appears confident his squad can compete for the trophy. His approach suggests he views tactical execution and team unity as the keys to success rather than relying on marquee individual players.

hero.headline: Jeremy Strong to Play Mark Zuckerberg in Social Network Sequel
hero.body:
Sony Pictures has unveiled the trailer for The Social Reckoning, a sequel to the 2010 Oscar-winning drama The Social Network. The film arrives sixteen years after the original chronicled Facebook's founding and early growth.

Jeremy Strong has been cast as Mark Zuckerberg in the new film, which examines the social media company through the lens of recent whistleblower revelations and internal investigations. Aaron Sorkin, who won the Oscar for best adapted screenplay on the first film, returns to write and direct the sequel. Sorkin previously signaled his political perspective on the project, stating: "I blame Facebook for January 6." He elaborated that the platform has been "tuning its algorithm to promote the most divisive material possible" and that there should be tension between growth and integrity at the company, but there isn't.

The original film, directed by David Fincher, won three Academy Awards and featured Jesse Eisenberg as the young Zuckerberg. It also starred Andrew Garfield, Justin Timberlake, Armie Hammer, and Rashida Jones. The 2010 film earned 224 million dollars worldwide.

The Social Reckoning shifts its focus from Facebook's creation to its later controversies. The sequel will be based on reporting by Jeff Horowitz for the Wall Street Journal in a series called The Facebook Files. That 2021 investigation exposed how internal findings had been buried and explored Facebook's influence on the January 6 riot and the mental health of teenage users.

Reports indicate that The Bear's Jeremy Allen White is in talks to play Horowitz, the journalist behind the investigation, while Anora's Mikey Madison would portray the whistleblower at the center of the articles. Madison recently won the Oscar for best actress in March.

Strong is known for his intense dramatic performances. He won an Emmy for his portrayal of Kendall Roy in the acclaimed HBO series Succession. He received an Oscar nomination this year for playing attorney Roy Cohn in The Apprentice, which traces the young Donald Trump's rise in 1980s New York. Strong will next appear alongside White in the Bruce Springsteen biopic Deliver Me from Nowhere, playing producer and Springsteen collaborator Jon Landau.

Zuckerberg himself was critical of the original Social Network in a recent podcast interview. "It was weird, man," he said. "They got all these very specific details of what I was wearing correct, but then the whole narrative arc around my motivations was completely wrong."

The original Social Network was based on the book The Accidental Billionaires by Ben Mezrich and became a cultural touchstone. The sequel represents Hollywood's continued fascination with the tech industry and its most prominent figures.

cards.headline: European Union Investigates Middle Eastern Funding in Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger
cards.teaser: The European Commission is examining approximately $24 billion in sovereign wealth fund backing for the proposed $111 billion entertainment merger.
cards.body:
The European Commission is examining Middle Eastern sovereign wealth fund involvement in Paramount Skydance's proposed takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery under the EU's Foreign Subsidies Regulation. The investigation focuses on approximately $24 billion in foreign government funding backing the $111 billion deal.

The merger would create one of the entertainment industry's largest conglomerates, combining major streaming services, studios, and sports broadcasting rights. The regulatory review will assess whether the foreign funding creates unfair competitive advantages in European markets.

cards.headline: Actor Tyler Mane Announces Breast Cancer Diagnosis
cards.teaser: The X-Men actor revealed he has been diagnosed with a rare form of breast cancer and is beginning chemotherapy treatment.
cards.body:
Tyler Mane, the 59-year-old actor and former professional wrestler best known for playing Sabretooth in the 2000 X-Men film, has revealed he has been diagnosed with breast cancer. He is currently undergoing chemotherapy treatment.

Mane shared the news on social media to raise awareness of the condition, which he described as rarely discussed. Male breast cancer accounts for only 1% of all breast cancer cases.

cards.headline: Comedian Adam Ray Launches Netflix Video Podcast
cards.teaser: The comedian will interview guests while performing as his roster of characters, including his popular Dr. Phil impression.
cards.body:
Adam Ray is launching a new Netflix video podcast called The Adam Ray Show, which will feature the comedian interviewing celebrities while portraying various characters. The show will debut on the streaming platform on June 19.

Ray plans to use his roster of character impressions throughout the podcast, including his well-known Dr. Phil persona. The format will combine traditional interview segments with Ray's comedic performances. Netflix is expanding its podcast offerings with the addition of Ray's character-based interview series.

cards.headline: Jennifer Lawrence Identified Leaker in Bravo Reality Show
cards.teaser: The actress helped discover who leaked information from the reality series Summer House, earning thanks from host Andy Cohen.
cards.body:
Jennifer Lawrence used her investigative skills to identify the person who leaked information from the Bravo reality series Summer House. Andy Cohen publicly thanked the actress during Watch What Happens Live after the final part of the Summer House finale aired.

Lawrence, described as a Bravo obsessive and part-time private investigator, successfully tracked down the source of leaks from the show. Cohen acknowledged her contribution during his late-night talk show. The actress is known among fans and industry insiders as a dedicated viewer of Bravo programming.

cards.headline: Brazilian Producer Joins Argentine Director's New Sci-Fi Project
cards.teaser: Rodrigo Teixeira's RT Features has signed on to Bodies of Summer, a new film from Berlin Film Festival award winner Iván Fund.
cards.body:
RT Features, the Brazilian production company behind 2025 Oscar winner I'm Still Here and James Gray's 2026 Cannes entry Paper Tiger, has joined Bodies of Summer as a producer. The sci-fi drama will be directed by Argentine filmmaker Iván Fund.

Fund won a Silver Bear Jury Prize at the 2025 Berlin Film Festival for his film The Message. Rodrigo Teixeira's company continues to expand its involvement in high-profile international productions.

cards.headline: German Producer Martin Moszkowicz Named Zurich Film Festival President
cards.teaser: The former Constantin Film chief executive will lead the Swiss festival alongside CEO Christian Jungen.
cards.body:
Martin Moszkowicz, the former chief executive of Constantin Film, has been appointed president of Zurich Film Festival. Moszkowicz will work with Christian Jungen, the festival's CEO, to advance the event's strategic goals.

As a producer, executive producer, and co-producer, Moszkowicz has been involved in more than 300 films throughout his career. He brings extensive experience in German and international film production to his new role at the Swiss festival. Moszkowicz and Jungen discussed their plans for the festival's future direction.

hero.headline: Trump warns Iran will pay the price as negotiations stall
hero.teaser: President Trump threatened consequences for Iran following attacks on U.S. allies Kuwait and Bahrain as nuclear negotiations drag on.
hero.body:
President Trump warned Iran on Wednesday morning that it will not get away with attacks on U.S. allies Kuwait and Bahrain. He posted on Truth Social that Iran has taken too long to negotiate a deal that would have been great for them, and now they will have to pay the price.

The warning comes as gas prices remain stuck above $4 per gallon. The stalled negotiations and regional tensions have contributed to sustained pressure on energy markets, affecting American consumers at the pump.

cards.headline: Trump signs immigration enforcement bill into law
cards.teaser: President Trump signed the Secure America Act into law Wednesday morning, finalizing a GOP-led reconciliation package that funds U.S.
cards.body:
President Trump signed the Secure America Act into law Wednesday morning, a GOP-led reconciliation package that funds U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Border Patrol through 2029. The nearly $70 billion bill passed the House on Tuesday and advanced in the Senate on Friday after weeks of negotiations among Republican leadership and party members.

The legislation allocates resources for personnel, detention facilities, and operational costs for both ICE and Border Patrol over the four-year period. Republicans argued the multi-year funding structure provides enforcement agencies with stable resources to conduct border security operations without relying on annual appropriations battles. Democrats opposed the package, citing concerns that the reconciliation process bypassed normal committee review and debate procedures.

cards.headline: Social Security commissioner testifies before House on agency oversight
cards.teaser: Social Security Administration Commissioner Frank Bisignano appeared before the House Ways and Means Committee to discuss agency operations.
cards.body:
Social Security Administration Commissioner Frank Bisignano testified Wednesday morning before the House Ways and Means Committee on oversight of the agency. The hearing focused on the agency's management and operational challenges.

The testimony came one day after the SSA released an annual report showing its Old-Age and Survivors Insurance Trust Fund will be able to pay 100 percent of its total scheduled benefits for a limited time period. The financial projections have renewed discussions about long-term solvency of the Social Security system.

cards.headline: Trump congratulates Graham on primary win, urges focus on voting legislation
cards.teaser: President Trump called on lawmakers to pass the SAVE America Act after Senator Lindsey Graham secured his Republican primary victory.
cards.body:
President Trump congratulated Senator Lindsey Graham on winning his South Carolina Republican primary on Tuesday, while calling for Congress to focus on passing the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act. Graham received nearly 60 percent of the vote against his primary challenger.

Trump used the occasion to push for the SAVE America Act, a voting legislation priority for his administration. Graham has been a key ally of the president in the Senate, supporting major administration initiatives and judicial nominations throughout Trump's term.

cards.headline: Trump attacks sports commentator Stephen A. Smith on social media
cards.teaser: President Trump called ESPN analyst Stephen A. Smith an arrogant fool following criticism over his attendance at an NBA Finals game.
cards.body:
President Trump attacked sports commentator Stephen A. Smith on Wednesday, calling the ESPN analyst an arrogant fool and a low IQ individual on his Truth Social platform. Trump wrote that Smith is dumb as a rock and totally unqualified to ever think of running for office.

The feud stems from Smith's comments on Tuesday that Trump should not have attended Game 3 of the NBA Finals on Monday. Smith told host Chris Cuomo that Trump should have stayed at the White House instead of appearing at the basketball game.

cards.headline: Bill Gates to testify before House panel in Epstein deposition
cards.teaser: Microsoft founder Bill Gates is scheduled to sit for a deposition with a House committee examining connections to Jeffrey Epstein.
cards.body:
Bill Gates is scheduled to testify before the House Committee on Oversight and Reform on Wednesday as part of an investigation into Jeffrey Epstein. The Microsoft co-founder will participate in a closed-door session where lawmakers plan to question him about his past relationship with the convicted sex offender. A transcript of the testimony is expected to be released later.

Gates has repeatedly denied any wrongdoing or knowledge of Epstein's illegal activities. He has previously acknowledged meeting with Epstein multiple times and described those interactions as focused on philanthropic discussions, though he has expressed regret about the relationship.

cards.headline: Lesley Stahl says Larry Ellison pledged editorial independence for 60 Minutes
cards.teaser: Veteran correspondent Lesley Stahl told colleagues she received assurances that 60 Minutes would retain editorial independence under new ownership.
cards.body:
Lesley Stahl, the veteran 60 Minutes correspondent who recently announced she would stay with the program, told colleagues this week she received assurances the news magazine show would remain independent under its corporate ownership. Stahl said Larry Ellison pledged to preserve the program's editorial autonomy as it undergoes organizational changes.

Stahl held a champagne toast in the 60 Minutes newsroom on Monday following the announcement. The longtime journalist's decision to remain with the program came amid uncertainty about the show's future direction under new management structure.
